chunks: Ali, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Follow the sequence in the wudu (ablution) just as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: Begin with the face, then with the hands, then wipe the head and the two feet, and do not bring forward anything before what you have been commanded to do; and if you washed the forearm before the face, then begin with the face and repeat upon the forearm; and if you wiped the foot before the head, then wipe upon the head before the foot, then repeat upon the foot. Begin with what Allah began with.'
ai.seo_question: What is the correct sequence for performing wudu and how to correct a mistake in order?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi explicitly codifies the Shia jurisprudential principle of *tartib* (sequential order) in ablution, deriving the specific sequence of washing the face, arms, wiping the head, and wiping the feet directly from the divine command in Surah al-Ma'idah. It provides a practical legal remedy for *nasi'* (delay) or *qadam* (premature action), requiring the believer to restart the sequence from the point of error to ensure ritual validity. This establishes that the order is not merely recommended but obligatory for the completeness of the act of worship.

en.hubeali: Ali, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fal Bin Shazaan, altogether from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Zurara who said,

‘Abu Ja’farasws sai: ‘There is a sequence between the Ablution (Wudhu) just as Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Said. Begin with the face, then with the two hands, then wipe the head and the two feet, and do not bring forward anything in front which was behind what you have been Commanded with; and if you were to wash the forearms before the face, so begin with the face and repeat upon the forearms; and if the man wipes the legs before the head, so he should wipe upon the head before the legs, then he should repeat upon the legs. Begin with what Allahazwj (has Asked one to) Begin with’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan all from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah who has said the following:

“Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘You must maintain the sequence in the acts of Wudu’ as Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has said. You must begin to wash your face, then wash your hands (forearms), then wipe your head and feet. You must not do any of such acts before what is next in the sequential order, which (is what) the command requires to maintain. If you wash your forearms before your face, you must begin with your face and wash your forearms again. If you wipe your feet before your head, you must wipe your head and then wipe your feet again. Begin with what Allah has said to begin with.’”
